abstract: Martin Goose is a process safety specialist who took early retirement from the Health and Safety Executive after 30 years dealing, primarily, with the major hazards sector. During his last 5 years with HSE he was head of the Major Hazards Assessment Unit and then the Process Safety Corporate Topic Group and Process Safety Specialist Pool. His last task within HSE was to be part of the Buncefield Investigation Team. He continues to be active in Safety and Loss Prevention as a committee member of the Institution of Chemical Engineers Subject Group on that topic, and in consultancy through WSAtkins and RPSrisk. Within the Institution of Chemical Engineers he is one of the panel of ChemEnvoys representing the profession to the media on major hazard safety issues.

Roger Rivett has worked in the automotive industry for over 28 years on real-time software for embedded-systems, particularly chassis and power-train systems. During this time he has fulfilled a number of different roles including software developer, Project Leader, Quality Manager and Functional Safety Technical Specialist.

Has spent ten years designing automatic flight control systems, and for the last twenty five years has been involved in the design and supply of Control and Safety systems for the process industry. Has been involved in projects for clients world wide, particularly in Europe, Middle East and America's Has published many articles concerning high integrity systems and is joint author of the book ‘Functional Safety’. Participates actively in various professional institutions and government safety committees relating to programmable electronic safety systems, and is a member of the international committee for both IEC 61508 (Generic Functional Safety standard for electrical based safety systems) and IEC 61511 (process industry sector specific of IEC 61508) and is a committee member of IGAS E Programmable Safety System.

Alan King is a Hazard and Reliability Specialist with ABB Engineering Services. He works with a wide range of companies across the process, nuclear, power generation, oil & gas, and manufacturing sectors.

Ron started his career as an engineering apprentice and gained experience in the manufacturing and telecommunications sectors before joining the Health and Safety Executive where he became the head of the Electrical and Control Systems Group. Andrew began his career in engineering as an Aircraft Technician (Propulsion) in the Royal Air Force. On completion of a 12-year engagement, he joined Rolls-Royce, writing nuclear safety justifications for submarine reactor instrumentation, control and protection systems. Andrew then moved into project management of nuclear safety for submarine and land-based reactor plant, and shore-side support facilities. Following a spell of Business Process Re-engineering, Andrew moved back into a technical role, compiling the safety case for the control panels in a new class of submarine manoeuvring room. This grew into a project leadership role, working with other defence companies on de-risking the acquisition of Platform Management Systems for future warships. In parallel, Andrew was seconded to another Rolls-Royce company as Project Manager for Type 45 Destroyer stabiliser and steering gear controls. Following the Rolls-Royce acquisition of the Vickers Ulstein group of companies, Andrew was a key figure in initiating and managing a project to work up an Industrial Design Manual to give all commercial marine product operator interfaces a common look and feel. Until recently, Andrew was responsible for the leadership and project management of a large part of a pan-European, 48-partner, four-year R&D project focused on improving the safety, environmental friendliness and competitiveness of European maritime transport. Andrew joined the new Rolls-Royce Civil Nuclear business at Easter this year, and is currently Programme Manager - In-Service Support. Through is career in engineering, Andrew has been registered as an Engineering Technician and an Incorporated Engineer, and is currently registered as a Chartered Engineer and a Chartered Manager.
